newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end with slump, Zurich gains.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end with slump, Zurich gains.

text.p: Heavy profit-taking, easing European stock prices and an early drop on Wall Street sent Swiss shares plummeting nearly two percent on Friday.
"The fear of a correction offset the good interest rate prospects," one dealer said, adding that investors were nervous given the recent record levels on the Swiss Exchange.

The market seemed split on whether the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) could hold the 5,000 point level next week. "This also depends on the outcome of French elections at the weekend, and, of course, Wall Street," one dealer said.
The SMI slid 90.5 points, or 1.76 percent, to 5,041.6. It had fallen as low as 5,027.3 during the session.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) lost 53.24 points, or 1.64 percent, to finish at 3,195.56.
Bourse volume was a moderate 2.433 billion francs.
One dealer said uncertainties stemming from Germany's plan to revalue Bundesbank gold reserves and its implications for Europe's single currency project were another cause for concern.

Insurer Zurich closed one franc higher at 520 following a New York Times report stating that the Swiss insurer was close to buying U.S. money management firm Scudder, Stevens & Clark. A Zurich spokeswoman declined comment.
Some financials apparently profited from easing Swiss interest rates as the Swiss National Bank kept offering liquidity to the market, one dealer said.
Actively traded Novartis registereds dropped 31 francs to 1,920. Zurich Cantonal Bank said the stocks were under technical pressure. Roche yielded 200 francs to 12,580.
CS Group was down 5.25 francs to 177.75. UBS bearers were down 19 francs at 1,552.
Temporary employment firm Adecco ended down seven francs at 532. The stocks traded ex-dividend of five francs.
Ciba SC slid 6.50 francs to 134 on downgrades.
